title: Bursts That Outlast Themselves: Persistent Degradation in Prefix-Cached Agent Serving
abstract: arXiv:2611.13412v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents drive inference engines with closed-loop sessions whose context grows every turn, and serving them economically depends on prefix caching: a hit costs an incremental prefill of about a thousand tokens, a miss recomputes a 10--40K-token context. We show that this makes prefix-cached agent serving metastable. With an identical base workload, a few minutes of extra arrivals leaves a vLLM server in a degraded regime--a ~10% hit ratio, about half the throughput, and a backlog that grows for the remaining 70 minutes--while its no-burst twin stays healthy (9 of 12 pairs; none in the reverse direction). The regime appears at loads the cache-warm server sustains, is absent without prefix caching, and also appears with Qwen3-32B on SWE-bench agent trace shapes and on SGLang, which tolerates larger triggers. Slower service keeps more sessions in the system, their working set outgrows the KV pool, and every turn becomes a recomputation;

translated_title: 比自身存在更久的突发：前缀缓存智能体服务中的持续性退化
translated_abstract: LLM 智能体以闭环会话的方式驱动推理引擎，其上下文在每一轮交互中不断增长，而经济高效地服务这类负载依赖于前缀缓存：缓存命中只需对约一千个 token 进行增量预填充，而缓存未命中则需要重新计算 10–40K token 的上下文。我们证明了这使前缀缓存的智能体服务呈现亚稳态特性。在相同的基础工作负载下，短短几分钟的额外到达请求就会使 vLLM 服务器进入退化状态——约 10% 的缓存命中率、大约一半的吞吐量，以及在剩余 70 分钟内持续增长的请求积压——而未经历突发的对照组服务器则保持健康（12 对实验中有 9 对出现此现象，反向情况则从未出现）。这种退化状态出现在缓存预热服务器本可承受的负载水平下，在没有前缀缓存时不会出现，并且在 Qwen3-32B 的 SWE-bench 智能体轨迹形态下以及 SGLang 系统上同样会出现（SGLang 仅能容忍更大的触发阈值）。变慢的服务使更多会话滞留在系统中，它们的工作集超出 KV 缓存池的容量，导致每一轮交互都退化为重新计算。
tldr: 本文发现前缀缓存的 LLM 智能体服务具有亚稳态特性：即使负载恢复，短短几分钟的请求突发也会使服务器陷入缓存命中率骤降至约 10%、吞吐量减半且持续恶化的退化状态，其根源是滞留会话的工作集超出 KV 缓存池，导致每轮交互都变成代价高昂的重新计算。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that prefix-cached LLM agent serving is metastable: even after load returns to baseline, a brief burst of a few minutes can trap the server in a persistent degraded regime with ~10% hit ratio and halved throughput, because lingering sessions' working sets outgrow the KV pool and every turn becomes a recomputation.
